4.text: forbidden on land, and allowed only on the river. The old men of both

5.text: tribes attributed this calamity to the increase of sinfulness in the world. There

6.text: is an old Yukaghir legend which aims at branding the wanton extermination

7.text: of game and fish. It relates how some men, in most versions some Russian

8.text: cossacks, tired of killing reindeer on the water, caught one, flayed it alive,

9.text: and allowed it to escape to the shore. Afterwards, in the fishing-season, they

10.text: took out the eyes of a live salmon, and in the same manner let it go free.

11.text: The next year, in hunting-time, the flayed reindeer was seen on the herd’s

12.text: trail, causing the herds to turn away from the river. Likewise the injured

13.text: salmon made the salmon-shoals go back to the sea, and a frightful famine

14.text: ensued. Up to a late period, when reindeer-herds or salmon-shoals were not

15.text: forthcoming, it was considered by the old people as a just punishment for the

16.text: reckless extermination of the game. It is true even at present, that the Chuk-

17.text: chee or Markova hunters, when successful, will kill much more than they want,

18.text: and afterwards take only the skins, at least from the lean animals, leaving

19.text: their carcasses to rot. The real reason that reindeer ceased to migrate in the

20.text: direction of Omolon and the two Anuis, however, probably lies in the fact

21.text: that the Reindeer Chukchee spread to the west, occupying the tundra pastures,

22.text: and so there was no place left for wild reindeer. On the upper course of the

29.text: On the Anadyr River the crossing-places of the reindeer are situated on

30.text: the middle part of the river, between the mouth of the Maïn and the small

31.text: Chukchee settlement Chikayeva. The reindeer leave the Palpal Mountains

32.text: about the middle of March, and keep crossing the river in bands of varying

33.text: numbers till the end of June. The greater portion, especially the pregnant dams,

34.text: cross before the ice breaks up. After having crossed the river, the reindeer

35.text: scatter all along the tundra. A large number remain in the Peˊkul-ñei Mountains,

37.text: and come back to the river; then the most important hunting-season begins.

38.text: Reindeer-herds take the same trail every year, and cross the river at the

39.text: same places. There the hunters, in separate groups, lie in ambush and wait

40.text: for the game, each tribe by itself. The Russianized natives keep watch more
